public_rationale: Three later independent studies document failures across classical reasoning puzzles, sequential state and relation tracking, and spatial rule execution. Together they satisfy the ordinary reading of many additional examples. This supports the existence forecast, not a claim that all models fail everywhere or that Apple's explanation of every failure is correct. The assessment depends on the stated reading of many.
limitations: The supporting records are public preprints; publication establishes that examples were reported, not universal acceptance of their explanations.
Task families overlap in broad computational demands and should not be added into a single supposedly independent example count.
Some models and configurations perform substantially better than others.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Many more examples of LLM/LRM failures at applying algorithms, like those in the Apple paper, will be uncovered.

statement.excerpt: I doubt any of them are perfect, but the four together provide converging evidence with dozens of other prior papers (including some of my own), and I am confident many more examples will be uncovered.
statement.document_title: Seven replies to the viral Apple reasoning paper – and why they fall short

from_speaker: many more examples will be uncovered
our_interpretation: The forecast concerns subsequently reported failures to apply rules or algorithms as task complexity, sequence length, or task variation increases.
Many more means a substantial collection across multiple independent studies and distinct task families, rather than numerous sampled failures of one puzzle.
This claim counts examples, not papers. It does not require every later study to endorse Apple's interpretation of why failures occur.
The accompanying statement about dozens of prior papers is not the forecast being assessed here.
criteria.support_condition: Post-publication empirical research documents a substantial collection of analogous failures across multiple independent studies and task families.
criteria.contradiction_condition: There is no finite-date contradiction from a shortage of examples because no deadline was stated. Evidence invalidating alleged examples would remove them from the supporting collection.

evidence.explanation: The published study reports complexity-related declines across nine validated reasoning tasks, including satisfiability, cryptarithmetic, graph coloring, water jugs, Sudoku, and Rubik's Cube. It supplies additional algorithmic and constraint-following examples beyond Apple's original task set.

The study evaluates spatial state tracking, symbolic pointer manipulation, and transitive inference while varying sequential depth. Its failures provide additional examples, although stronger models retain substantial performance in some domains.

Grid-Bench tests explicit rules across eight spatial-operation families with executable reference answers. Together with e1 and e2, it establishes a substantial collection of later failures across distinct tasks and independent research teams.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: By this publication, e1–e3 collectively document a substantial collection across multiple independent studies and distinct task families, meeting the stated positive-resolution rule.
